**TL;DR** — The big actionable item today is a critical, actively-exploited Gitea vulnerability (CVE-2026-59774, CVSS 9.8) letting unauthenticated attackers read arbitrary files and potentially reach RCE — patch to 1.27.1 now if you're self-hosting Gitea.

## Anthropic and Claude
- Claude Code v2.1.224–2.1.226 (Aug 7–8) — self-hosted environments (`claude self-hosted-runner`), cross-session messaging via a new `SendMessage` tool, gateway spend-limit support, workspace trust prompts, and sandbox credential masking. [changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- "Improving Fable 5's biology safeguards" (Aug 7) — Anthropic tightened bio-risk safety features on the Fable 5 model. [Anthropic News](https://www.anthropic.com/news)
- Tino Cuéllar named Chief Global Affairs Officer (Aug 4) — new exec hire, not a technical change but signals continued policy/gov't-relations buildout. [Anthropic News](https://www.anthropic.com/news)
- Boris Cherny (Claude Code lead) on rewriting a desktop app in Swift with Claude over 14+ days (Aug 2) — a real account of long-horizon agentic coding, likened to pixel-by-pixel verification work; linked from Daring Fireball. [Daring Fireball](https://daringfireball.net/)
- Claude Opus 5 remains the frontier release (shipped Jul 24, ongoing) — 1M context, $10/$50 per Mtok, aimed at long-running coding agents. [Anthropic News](https://www.anthropic.com/news)

## NixOS ecosystem
- Nixpkgs core team disbanded (Aug 7) — the two-member team cited burnout and Steering Committee dysfunction ("lacks a native instinct for the delegation envisioned by the constitution"); core responsibilities revert to the SC with no direct owner for now. Worth watching ahead of the upcoming SC election. **Outside approved set** (discourse.nixos.org, not nixos.org/blog). [NixOS Discourse](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/the-nixpkgs-core-team-has-disbanded/79413)
- No new posts on nixos.org/blog in the last 7 days — most recent is the documentation-funding initiative (Jul 10) and NixOS 26.05 "Yarara" (May 30), both still the current state of play. [NixOS Blog](https://nixos.org/blog/)

## AI coding agents and agent frameworks
- Meta launched Muse Code (Aug 5) — a terminal coding agent for large repos, built on Muse Spark, with steep pricing discounts ($0.10/$0.20 vs $1.25/$4.25 per Mtok) tied to data-sharing opt-in — notable as a direct Claude Code/Codex competitor with an unusual pricing lever. **Outside approved set.** [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/05/meta-launches-muse-code-an-ai-agent-for-large-code-bases/)
- Claude Code's shift to background-by-default subagents and cross-session `SendMessage` (see above) is itself a notable agent-framework development this week. [changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)

## Self-hosting and homelab
- Critical Gitea RCE-adjacent flaw, CVE-2026-59774 / GHSA-6v53-hr58-556r (advisory Aug 2, CVSS 9.8) — unauthenticated attackers can abuse Org-mode `#+INCLUDE` in the markup endpoint to read arbitrary files (e.g. `app.ini`, extracting `INTERNAL_TOKEN`), chaining to RCE via a malicious Git hook; affects 1.22.1–1.27.0, fixed in 1.27.1, exploitation reported in the wild. Patch immediately. **Outside approved set** — official GitHub Security Advisory. [GHSA-6v53-hr58-556r](https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/security/advisories/GHSA-6v53-hr58-556r)
- Proxmox VE 9.2 ships official Arm64 support (Aug 5) — full KVM/LXC/ZFS/Ceph feature parity on Arm, relevant if you're building a low-power homelab node. **Outside approved set.** [elest.io roundup](https://blog.elest.io/self-hosted-weekly-week-32-2026-proxmox-arm64-rust-ai-policy-gitea-cve/) (unverified against Proxmox's own release notes — treat as unverified)

## Local and on-device LLM inference
- Nothing new surfaced from the approved sources or in general search this week — llama.cpp (~118k stars, 900+ contributors) and Ollama (~169k stars, 2.5B+ model pulls) remain the dominant runtime/front-end pairing (ongoing), and Q4_K_M-class GGUF quantization is still the practical sweet spot for 70B-class models on consumer hardware (ongoing). No release-worthy news to report today.
